WA-2025-SB6228.title: Removing a tax exemption for the warehousing and reselling of prescription drugs.
WA-2025-SB6228.summary:
The preferential B&O tax rate of 0.138 percent for warehousing and reselling of prescription drugs is repealed. Beginning January 1, 2027, the gross income of businesses warehousing and reselling drugs for human use pursuant to a prescription is subject to a B&O tax rate of 0.5 percent.

The term "warehousing and reselling drugs for human use pursuant to a prescription" is defined in the bill as the buying of drugs for human use pursuant to a prescription from a manufacturer or another wholesaler and reselling of the drugs to persons selling at retail or to hospitals, clinics, health care providers, or other providers of health care services by a wholesaler or retailer who is registered with the federal Drug Enforcement Administration and licensed by the state Pharmacy Quality Assurance Commission.

WA-2025-HB2548.title: Strengthening health care market standards.
WA-2025-HB2548.summary:
Notice of Material Change .

The following additional transactions qualify as material changes that trigger the 60-day notice requirement for certain transactions involving health care market participants:
• a transaction involving any entity or person that results in a change of majority ownership or control of a hospital, hospital system, or provider organization;
• an acquisition, sale, or transfer of the majority of the assets of a hospital, hospital system, or provider organization, including real property sale and leaseback transactions; and
• a conversion of a hospital, hospital system, or provider organization from a nonprofit corporation to a for-profit corporation or unincorporated entity.

The written notice must include the name of any person or entity with a majority ownership, investment, or controlling interest of any party. The parties must provide notice of the completion of the transaction to the Attorney General within 30 days after the transaction is completed.

The Attorney General must make public on its website a quarterly notice of pending and completed material change transactions. The Attorney General must notify the Secretary of State when an entity involved in specified material change transactions is a nonprofit corporation.

Requests for Additional Information .

If the Attorney General requests additional information from the parties to a material change transaction, the transaction may not proceed until 30 days after the parties have certified they are in substantial compliance with the request. Any subsequent request for additional information will not extend the 30-day waiting period for the parties to close the transaction.

Filing Fees .

Parties filing a written notice of a material change transaction must pay a filing fee. Only one filing fee is required per transaction. Filing fees are assessed based on the anticipated value of the transaction in Washington. Parties to a contracting affiliation between a state-owned or state-operated entity and a public hospital district are not required to pay the filing fee.

The Attorney General may index the filing fee amounts in accordance with the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index for medical care. All receipts from filing fees must be deposited in the Antitrust Revolving Fund.

WA-2025-HB2405.title: Establishing a pilot program for posttraumatic stress disorder treatment and research.
WA-2025-HB2405.summary:
Use of Safety and Health Investment Return-to-Work Program Funds. L&I is authorized to use the funds allocated for effective return-to-work projects related to return-to-work programs to provide funding for grants or contracts for the development and evaluation of workplace behavioral health programs including, but not limited to, suicide prevention, mental health training, trauma-informed reintegration protocols, independent navigator programs, and developing supportive workplace cultures. The projects must be focused on occupations that have high risk of PTSD through repetitive exposure to trauma. L&I may determine appropriate organizations eligible for awards.

Pilot Program for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Occupational Disease Claims. In consultation with experts from L&I and advisory committees including, the Workers' Compensation Advisory Committee, L&I must design and implement a pilot program to expand access to evidence-based, high quality care for workers exposed to trauma seeking coverage of PTSD as an occupational disease. Self-insurers may choose to participate in the pilot program.

Worker Participation in the Pilot. As part of the pilot program, when a worker files an occupational disease claim for PTSD, L&I or participating self-insurer must provide the worker the opportunity to participate in the pilot program. If the worker opts for their claim to be part of the pilot program, L&I or participating self-insurers must authorize access to treatment for PTSD prior to claim adjudication, without regard to whether the worker's claim for benefits is allowed. Workers may receive the preclaim adjudication treatment from a qualified mental health provider if the provider agrees to be paid in accordance with the department's medical aid rules and fee schedules and signs a nonnetwork provider agreement. L&I will survey or contact these providers to better understand barriers to entering the medical provider network.

Cost of Treatment Under the Pilot. Costs for treatment prior to claim adjudication on state fund claims that are ultimately rejected will be spread across all risk classes for which there is a presumption of coverage of PTSD as an occupational disease. Costs for treatment prior to claim adjudication on self-insured claims that are ultimately rejected will be paid by the self-insurer. Payment for this treatment or any other benefits, prior to the entry of an L&I order must not be considered a binding determination of the L&I or the self-insurer's obligations.

If the claim has not been adjudicated for allowance within 90 days, the supervisor of industrial insurance may authorize continued treatment of up to 12 treatment sessions. WA-2025-HB1701.title: Authorizing multiple liquor licensees to have licensed premises within a facility owned and leased out by another liquor licensee or person.
WA-2025-HB1701.summary:
Liquor Licensing. The bill provides that an applicant may be licensed to operate from a premises located on the property of a facility that contains separate premises of other liquor licensees or other businesses.

The owner of the facility may be, but is not required to be, one of the licensees operating a premises at the facility. A licensee who owns real property, or real and personal property, may lease that property to other licensees or businesses operating their own premises at the facility.

A licensee may lease use of its kitchen to another person. Before operating from the leased kitchen, the licensee must ensure the lessee holds all required permits, approvals, and licenses, including applicable food service permits and state and local business licenses.

LCB may not consider the existence of leasing arrangements authorized in the bill to affect a licensee's ownership and control of its premises or otherwise prevent licensure. LCB may require submission of lease agreements, operating agreements, and other contracts between the facility owner, licensees, and businesses operating at the facility to ensure each licensee retains ownership and control of its licensed premises. Each licensee and business must operate from its own premises on the facility property, except as otherwise authorized by law and for leased use of kitchen facilities.

The bill specifies that nothing in the bill:
• authorizes a licensee to engage in privileges not authorized under the terms of the license;
• requires a licensee to obtain a liquor license for an activity conducted by another licensee from that other licensee's separate premises at the facility;
• authorizes business practices or financial arrangements that are otherwise prohibited under state liquor law, including restrictions on industry members providing money or things of value to retailers;
• authorizes a person who does not hold a liquor license to engage in an activity that requires holding a liquor license; or
• authorizes a person, including a lessee of a kitchen, to engage in food preparation or service without holding all required permits, approvals, and licenses.

Tied-House Restrictions. The bill creates an exception to provisions governing financial interests between industry members and retailers to allow a person holding a domestic brewery, microbrewery, domestic winery, distillery, craft distillery, or manufacturer's license to operate a premises in a facility where a person holding a retail liquor license also operates in a separate space. The facility may be owned by any of these licensees and space may be leased to other such licensees, consistent with the facility provisions established in the bill.

WA-2025-HB2339.title: Concerning the regulation of nursing.
WA-2025-HB2339.summary:
Advanced Registered Nurse Practitioner Titles .

All ARNPs may use the title "advanced registered nurse practitioner" and abbreviation "ARNP." Each practitioner type may use the title of their specific designation and corresponding abbreviation: certified nurse practitioner or CNP, certified nurse midwife or CNM, certified registered nurse anesthetist or CRNA, and certified clinical nurse specialist or CCNS. A person not licensed as an ARNP may not use these titles.

Advanced registered nurse practitioners may also use the title "advanced practice registered nurse" or "APRN," which will become the license's official title pursuant to previously enacted legislation, effective June 30, 2027.

Administration of Controlled Substances by Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists .

Certified registered nurse anesthetists who have not obtained prescriptive authority prior to July 1, 2026, may continue to select, order, and administer controlled substances in a manner consistent with their scope of practice, subject to a request by certain licensed health care providers and to facility-specific protocols.

Application Requirements for Nursing Licenses .

Applicants for licensure as a registered nurse, ARNP, or licensed practical nurse no longer need to submit nursing program transcripts to the Board.

Issuance of Interim Permits .

The Board may issue an interim permit authorizing an applicant to practice registered nursing, advanced registered nursing, or licensed practical nursing during the period of time between verification of the applicant's completion of their training program and receipt of licensing examination results.

WA-2025-HB2229.title: Concerning the professional engineers' registration act.
WA-2025-HB2229.summary:
The Board of Registration for Professional Engineers and Land Surveyors . The requirement for each member of the Board to be a citizen of the United States is removed. A requirement is added that each member of the Board must have practiced professional engineering or professional land surveying in Washington for at least five years immediately preceding the member's appointment to the Board.

The number of authorized pro tem Board members is increased from two to three, and the process for their approval and appointment is revised. Upon request of the Board, the Director would select a candidate for a pro tem Board member position and upon approval of the Board, the Board Chair would make the appointment, instead of the Director approving and the Board Chair appointing individuals to serve as pro tem members.

Pro tem Board members may also perform services as needed and determined by the Director, including ensuring sufficient case reviewers and forming a quorum at Board meetings. An appointed individual must be registered under the Act or licensed in Washington to perform design services for on-site wastewater treatment systems for a minimum of five years immediately prior to the appointment, instead of being required to meet the same qualifications as regular members of the Board.

Roster Information. A requirement for the information in a roster of all registered professional engineers and land surveyors is changed so that the mailing address, not the place of business, must be shown in the roster.

Registration Requirements. The requirements considered as minimum evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant is qualified for registration as a professional engineer, structural engineer, professional land surveyor, engineer-in-training, and land-surveyor-in-training are modified. The eight years of experience must be broad-based and progressive to include, for professional engineers, gaining knowledge and comprehension of engineering subjects and applying engineering principles, and for professional land surveyors, applying land surveying principles. An undergraduate degree in a non-engineering program may, at the Board's discretion, be considered the equivalent of four years of engineering experience, instead of being limited to two years of the experience. An undergraduate degree equivalent to a land surveying program approved by the Board is also considered the equivalent of four years of the land surveying experience. Experience may be granted for teaching and postgraduate education as further defined by, and at the discretion of, the Board, instead of teaching of a character satisfactory to the Board being considered up to two years of experience, and postgraduate experience being considered up to one year of experience.

WA-2025-SB6019.title: Improving the functioning of home care rate statutes.
WA-2025-SB6019.summary:
The bill as referred to committee not considered.

Summary of Bill (First Substitute):
Home care agency vendor rate as being equal to the sum of the home care agency administrative rate and the vendor rate portion dedicated to the wages, benefits, and required employer contributions or premiums for home care agency workers who provide direct care.

DSHS shall determine, in its sole discretion, the total vendor rate portion dedicated to wages, benefits, and required employer contributions for home care agency workers who provide direct care for fiscal year 2027.

Beginning in fiscal year 2028, the total vendor rate portion dedicated to wages, benefits, and required employer contributions or premiums for home care agency workers who provide direct care is equal to the total portion from the previous fiscal year plus the incremental change that is calculated within the current existing process.

The vendor rate portion calculated for training may only be used for training, testing, and certification costs, and associated costs for the administration of training, testing, and certification scheduling and compliance for home care agency workers who provide direct care.

Verification of Funds. Beginning July 1, 2027, DSHS, or its designee, must verify that home care agencies have expended funds for the wages and benefits, health care rate, and training rate requirements. To assist DSHS, or its designee, with the verification of funds, each home care agency must submit to DSHS:
• an independent third-party audit conducted by a qualified, accredited firm to validate compliance with the established requirements; or
• a written attestation from the labor organizations that is the exclusive bargaining representative of the home care workers who provide direct care that are employed by the agency, confirming that the home care agency has complied with the wages and benefits, health care rate, and training rate requirements.

DSHS may adopt rules to establish reasonable objective criteria to temporarily exempt a home care agency determined to be facing extraordinary circumstances that prevent the compliance with the fund verification process. DSHS must develop the criteria through a transparent process that includes public notice and public comment opportunities for interested parties.

Home Care Agency Administrative Rate. DSHS must determine a home care agency administrative rate, which is the portion of the home care agency vendor rate designated to support the home care agency's administrative functions and essential operations. These functions and operations may include but are not limited to:
• compliance with administrative requirements related to Department of Health licensing and DSHS contracts for personal care and respite services;
• payment of all taxes and costs associated with obtaining and maintaining a licensed business in the state of Washington, as well as compliance with all labor and industry, local, state, and federal standards and…

WA-2025-SB6091.title: Prohibiting real estate brokers from marketing residential properties to an exclusive group of prospective buyers or real estate brokers.
WA-2025-SB6091.summary:
Requirement to Publicly Market Residential Real Estate. A broker may not market the sale or lease of residential real estate to a limited or exclusive group of prospective buyers or brokers, or any combination thereof, unless the real estate is concurrently marketed to the general public and all other brokers, except as reasonably necessary to protect the health or safety of the owner or occupant.

Marketing to the general public does not require an owner to allow access onto the residential real estate or into the residence.

Information regarding the requirement must be included in a pamphlet currently required to be provided by brokers to their principals.

A violation of the requirement is subject to disciplinary action by the Washington State Department of Licensing.

WA-2025-SB6080.title: Concerning contracts between the United States and county and municipal jails for committing or confining individuals in federal custody.
WA-2025-SB6080.summary:
Allows a person in charge of a jail to choose to receive and keep in the jail, when room is available, a person that is confined or committed by process or order issued under the authority of the United States pursuant to a contract.

A jail, in it's discretion, may confine or commit an individual in federal custody, prior to creation of a contract. The jail must create a contract with the United States to confine or commit a person within 180 days of first accepting a person in federal custody. During the 180 day period of creating the contract, the jail may continue to accept individuals in federal custody.

Any contract created must establish a fee at a rate of at least the daily bed rate established by interlocal agreement.

Clarifies that a jail is not prevented from accepting a person in federal custody for confinement or commitment if the jail determines that there is a reasonable public safety interest in accepting such person.
WA-2025-SB6080.summarySource: Washington Legislature Senate bill report (6080-S SBR APS 26, 2026-02-17)

WA-2025-SB6080.aiSummary: The bill would let county and city jails choose to hold people in federal custody when space is available. A jail could do this before a contract is in place, but it would have to make a contract with the United States within 180 days of first taking such a person. The contract would need to set a fee of at least the daily bed rate agreed to by local governments, and a jail could also accept someone if it finds a public safety reason to do so.

WA-2025-SB5931.title: Concerning workforce education investment accountability and oversight board administrative changes.
WA-2025-SB5931.summary: The WEIAO Board members must elect cochairs biennially, and those cochairs serve for two-year terms. The WEIAO Board must meet at least four times a year, and report recommendations to the Legislature by December 31 of each year. In addition to consulting with the Workforce Training and Education Coordinating Board, the WEIAO Board must also consult with the WSAC when reviewing and determining whether workforce education investments funded from the Workforce Education Investment Account are effectively increasing student success and career readiness. The requirement that the WEIAO Board maintain a public data dashboard is eliminated.
WA-2025-SB5931.summarySource: Washington Legislature House bill report (5931-S HBR PEW 26, 2026-02-27)

It would require the board to pick co-chairs every two years, meet at least four times a year, and send yearly recommendations to the Legislature by December 31. The board would also have to consult with the Washington Student Achievement Council when reviewing whether these education investments are helping students succeed and get ready for jobs, and it would no longer have to keep a public data dashboard.
